govt_response.summary: The ministry records that the statutory right covers ages 6-14 and that secondary schooling was being expanded through RMSA rather than a constitutional right.

analysis:
On 4 December 2009, HRD Minister Kapil Sibal said the government hoped to make free and compulsory education a right at the secondary stage by 2013 or 2015, after the RTE Act had made elementary education a fundamental right.

The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act 2009 and Article 21A apply to children aged six to fourteen years. Secondary education was being expanded through a scheme, the Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan, not through a legal entitlement.

No law extending the right to secondary education was enacted during the 2009-2014 period, and the stated 2013/2015 window passed without such a right coming into force.
notes: The claim is a hope framed with a conditional deadline ('hopefully by 2013 or 2015'). A dedicated source confirming that no secondary-education right was enacted was not located; the verdict rests on the statutory scope of the RTE Act described in PIB releases.
